sites.desc: The fort, also called Al Ali Fort, was built in 1768 by Sheikh Rashid bin Majid Al Mualla, founder of the modern Al Mualla dynasty, in the old town of Umm Al Quwain. It was the seat of the rulers and centre of government until 1969, and on 9 February 1929 Sheikh Hamad bin Ibrahim Al Mualla was killed inside it, after which townspeople set fire to its walls. It later served as a police station and was restored and opened to the public in 2000 by Sheikh Rashid bin Ahmed Al Mualla. It now houses the Umm Al Quwain National Museum, whose exhibits include artefacts from the archaeological site of Ed-Dur.

sites.el: 2,950 km²; water table less than 1 m below the surface
sites.te: The salt flat that drinks from below
sites.se: A vast salt flat runs about 150 km south from the western Abu Dhabi coast, where salty groundwater rises and dries in the sun

sites.desc: Sabkhat Matti is described as the largest inland sabkha in the Arabian Peninsula, covering 2,950 km² and extending about 150 km south from the western Abu Dhabi coastline into the Rub' al Khali, across the border between the UAE and Saudi Arabia. Its water table lies less than 1 m below the surface, so groundwater evaporates directly, and the drainage area supporting it exceeds 250,000 km². A groundwater and solute-budget study estimated that about 95% of its dissolved salts come from brine rising from the underlying regional aquifers, and gave the sabkha an age of roughly 8,000 to 5,000 years. Its lowest point is reported at 17 m below sea level.
sites.sig: A natural laboratory for how inland salt flats grow from rising groundwater in a hyper-arid desert.

sites.desc: Jebel Dhanna, near Ruwais, is described as the only exposed salt dome in onshore Abu Dhabi. The elliptical dome, elongated north–south, measures about 2–2.8 km east–west and 3.2–4.2 km north–south, and a series of hills rises about 110 m above sea level, with tilted Upper Miocene and Quaternary strata around and within it. The British Geological Survey mapped it with the island domes and found it to be a multiple-phase diapir; the UAE domes expose the Hormuz Complex, a clay-rich gypsum–anhydrite breccia whose volcanic rocks are dated to about 560 Ma. Current research studies the Hormuz salt here for large-scale hydrogen and hydrocarbon storage.
sites.sig: It brings Ediacaran salt from many kilometres down to the surface of the Abu Dhabi mainland and is a reference site for salt tectonics and energy storage.

sites.desc: Sir Bani Yas, an island of 87 km² stretching 17.5 km from north to south off the Al Dhafra coast, is the crest of a salt dome. Its central hills are remnants of the dome and include haematite outcrops that rise above the surrounding land and sea. It is one of eight diapiric islands in the UAE sector of the Arabian Gulf that owe their origin to the upward movement of Infra-Cambrian to Cambrian salt; the British Geological Survey groups the dome rocks as the Hormuz Complex, whose volcanic rocks are dated to about 560 Ma. In 1971 Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan declared the island a nature reserve, now the Arabian Wildlife Park covering 1,400 hectares.

sites.se: On this low coastal hill, rocks laid down by rivers 6 to 8 million years ago hold the bones of a small extinct hippo

sites.desc: Jebel Barakah is a hill on the Al Dhafra coast that exposes the Baynunah Formation, laid down six to eight million years ago when a complex of wide rivers crossed western Abu Dhabi. It is one of the localities, with Shuwaihat, Jebel Dhanna, Ruwais, Gerain Al Aysh and Jebel Mimiyah near Mirfa, that yielded the bones of Archaeopotamus qeshta, a hippopotamus named in 2017 from material collected from 1988 onwards, including by Peter Whybrow of the Natural History Museum, London. The study links the species to an evolutionary event about 8 million years ago and to dispersal through Arabia about 7.5 to 6.5 million years ago. The wider Baynunah fauna includes four-tusked elephants, several giraffes, six antelope species, crocodiles, three kinds of turtle and at least three kinds of fish.

sites.sa: على جزيرة في أقصى الغرب بنت أسر من الصيادين بيوتًا حجرية مستديرة قبل 8,500 عام، ثم رحلت حين قسا المناخ
sites.desc: Ghagha Island, about 5 km² and linked by a bridge to Ras Ghumais, holds the earliest known buildings in the UAE. In 2022 the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi reported simple round rooms with stone walls preserved to nearly 1 m, dated by radiocarbon on charcoal to at least 8,500 years ago, with finely worked stone arrowheads; a person was buried in the ruins nearly 5,000 years ago. The neighbouring site GHG0088, published in 2025, has two Early Neolithic phases (about 6600–5400 cal. BCE): stone buildings with a grave and a fishing economy, then, after a layer of wind-blown sand possibly linked to the 8.2 ka cooling event, reuse of the collapsed buildings as a fishing camp. Finds include plaster vessels, shell tools and beads of Engina mendicaria, a shell from waters at least 500 km away.
sites.sig: It pushes back stone architecture in the Arabian Gulf by at least 500 years and shows how an early island community responded to climate change.
sites.ex: DCT Abu Dhabi (2022); Lidour et al. (2025), PLOS ONE

sites.s: 7,000-year-old village with Ubaid pottery and early dates · later a pearl-trading town
sites.dr: Date stones 5500–4500 BCE; pearl trade peak 1880s–1890s; mosques 1931 and 1946
sites.te: The island of dates and pearls
sites.se: Seven thousand years ago the people of Dalma ate dates, gathered pearl oysters and owned pottery brought from distant Mesopotamia
sites.sa: قبل سبعة آلاف عام أكل سكان دلما التمر وجمعوا محار اللؤلؤ، واقتنوا فخارًا جُلب من بلاد الرافدين البعيدة
sites.desc: Dalma (Delma) lies off the Al Dhafra coast and measures about 5 km from north to south and 5 km from east to west; freshwater wells made settlement possible. The Abu Dhabi Islands Archaeological Survey identified more than 20 sites in 1992, and a house of the first inhabitants, about 7,000 years old, yielded Ubaid pottery imported from Mesopotamia, local plaster copies decorated with haematite and many pearl-oyster shells. Charred date stones dated to between 5500 and 4500 BCE are among the earliest evidence of date consumption in the Arabian Peninsula. In the 1880s and 1890s Dalma was an important pearl-trading centre; its three historic mosques include Al Dawsari (1931) and Al Muhannadi (1946), and the merchant house Bait Al Muraykhi now holds the Delma Museum.
sites.sig: Some of the earliest evidence in Arabia for eating dates and for contact with Ubaid Mesopotamia, on an island that remained a pearling hub into the 20th century.

sites.s: Fenced 774 km² desert reserve in Baynunah · houbara breeding habitat and oryx releases
sites.te: A safe home for the houbara
sites.se: In the Baynunah desert a fenced reserve protects the breeding grounds of the houbara bustard, and Arabian oryx have been set free here
sites.sa: في صحراء بينونة تحمي محمية مسيّجة مواطن تكاثر طائر الحبارى، وفيها أُطلق المها العربي إلى البرية
sites.desc: Al Houbara Protected Area lies in Baynunah in the Al Dhafra region and was established in 2008 to protect natural habitats suitable for breeding of the houbara bustard. The reserve covers 774 km², is completely fenced and is managed by the Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi. In November 2020 the agency began releasing Arabian oryx here, the first of 100 to be released in stages under the Sheikh Mohamed Bin Zayed Arabian Oryx Reintroduction Programme. The reserve hosts one of the region's most significant houbara reintroduction programmes, and the sand cat was recorded there after a long absence.
sites.sig: It protects breeding habitat for the houbara bustard and gives reintroduced Arabian oryx space in western Abu Dhabi.

sites.s: Largest island off the UAE coast · crab-plover colony, mangroves and wader flats
sites.dr: Important Bird Area (assessed 2017); Abu Al Abyad Marine Reserve designated 2025
sites.el: Island of 306 km²; IBA of 600 km²
sites.se: On the largest island off the UAE coast, crab plovers nest in a protected colony while thousands of waders feed on the tidal flats
sites.sa: على كبرى الجزر قبالة ساحل الإمارات يعشّش زقزاق السرطان في مستعمرة محمية، وتقتات آلاف الطيور الخوّاضة على السهول المدّية
sites.desc: Abu Al Abyad is the largest of about 200 islands along the UAE coast, covering 306 km². BirdLife International describes a large, low-lying island of calcareous sands and sabkha with extensive intertidal sandflats and mature Avicennia mangroves. Its baseline account records a breeding colony of 200–300 pairs of crab plovers (Dromas ardeola), probably about 280, inside a fenced private reserve of about 20 ha, and peak passage-wader counts of more than 6,000 birds; green turtles are numerous inshore and bottlenose and humpback dolphins are common. In October 2025 the Abu Al Abyad Marine Reserve was designated as part of an expansion of Abu Dhabi's protected areas.
sites.sig: A key breeding site for the crab plover and a major stopover for migrating waders on the Arabian Gulf coast.
